title: DR1 shows an identification task only when the chosen commodity has identifiers to give; the frontend always shows one, so a user is told to identify animals the service will not ask them about.

finding.frontend: 'Animal identification details' is an unconditional task row (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:41-45): it has no conditional flag, so the hub renders it whatever commodity has been chosen, and whether or not one has been chosen at all. The captured hub is of a notification with no commodity details filled in and the row is there, reading 'Not yet started'.
finding.prototype: DR1 adds its 'Identification details' task only when at least one chosen species has identifier fields defined for it (app/routes.js:5777-5781, and the test at :1489-1493). With no species chosen, or with a species that has no identifiers, the task is simply not in the list — which is why the captured DR1 hub shows two tasks in 'Description of the goods' and not three. A DR1 user is never shown an identification task they have nothing to put in.
finding.difference: Make the identification task conditional on the chosen commodity actually calling for identifiers, so it disappears from the hub when it does not apply — the hub already has the machinery for this, since the exit-details and transit-countries rows are declared conditional and drop out when their answers are out of scope. What the identification page itself should ask of a commodity with no typed identifiers is a separate finding on that page.
finding.falsifiedBy: A DR1 hub showing an 'Identification details' task on a notification whose chosen species has no identifier fields.

relatedTo.why: the same task is also named differently on the two sides
